title: Why did America build a canal, then give it away?

post.caption: The World's Chokepoints: the Panama Canal. The French failure, the 1903 Canal Zone, the 1914 opening, the 1977 treaties and the 1999 handover. Images: public domain (BnF, Library of Congress, US National Archives, US Navy, White House). Map data: Natural Earth.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Why did America build a canal, then give it away?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: The Panama Canal joins two oceans. Since 1999, it has belonged to Panama.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Where exactly is it?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: It crosses Panama near its narrowest point, from Colón to Panama City.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Eighty-two kilometres of locks, hills and a huge artificial lake.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Why does it matter so much?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Before it, ships from New York to San Francisco sailed around South America. The canal cut the trip by more than half.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Who tried first?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: France. In 1881, Ferdinand de Lesseps, the man behind the Suez Canal, started digging.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Yellow fever and malaria killed about twenty thousand workers. In 1889, the company went bankrupt.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Then America stepped in?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1903, Panama broke away from Colombia, backed by American warships. The United States got a strip across it: the Canal Zone.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: The Americans fought the mosquitoes and cut through a mountain range. Still, about five thousand six hundred workers died.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: On the fifteenth of August 1914, the ship Ancon made the first official crossing.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: So how did Panama get it back?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: After years of protests, Jimmy Carter and Omar Torrijos signed treaties in 1977 to hand it over.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: At noon on the last day of 1999, the canal became Panamanian.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And today?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Each ship uses millions of litres of lake water. In a drought, fewer ships get through.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 2025, Donald Trump said America would take it back. Panama said it will stay Panamanian.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Next time: Greenland. Like the video and follow History Sketches.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And tell us in the comments what you think!
